HOME SCIENCE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #6
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: HOME SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Methods of Cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Methods of Cooking.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Methods of Cooking.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Methods of Cooking.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Methods of Cooking.

   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Producers

   D. Decomposers only

9. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

10. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Kitchen Layouts and Equipment? (1 mark)

   B. Only water vapour
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Nitrogen gas only

15. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

16. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Heating until a solid melts

17. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 100 °C

18. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)

   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. newton (N)
   D. watt (W)

   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Overgrazing continuously
